# Paint font fixtures

`moli-text-stroke.ttf` is original project test data licensed under MIT OR
Apache-2.0. Regenerate it with `uv run scripts/generate-text-stroke-test-font.py`.
Its triangle glyphs have miter ratios below and above 4, distinguishing miter
joins from round joins and checking the bevel fallback at the miter limit.
Glyph C has a negative left side bearing that differs from its raw `glyf`
bounds, checking that allocation uses the rendered glyph's origin.
Glyphs D and E are closed vertical/horizontal lines with zero fill area but
visible stroke ink; the space glyph has no path at all.
Glyph R is a rectangle for checking synthetic weight and both sides of its
stroke. `moli-text-stroke-250.ttf` has the same shapes at UPEM 250, compared
against the UPEM 1000 font to test the local CSS pixel contract.
`moli-text-stroke-svg.ttf` preserves those outlines and adds an OpenType SVG
record only for R. It checks PDF fallback to the rectangle when the SVG renderer
is unavailable, both alone and next to ordinary outline glyphs.
`moli-text-stroke-colr.ttf` adds a COLR v0 rectangle for A with a 50% red
palette entry, retaining its base outline. `moli-text-stroke-colr-svg.ttf`
adds the independent SVG record for R to the same font. Actual PDF reader
regressions check that neither semantic text, fill/stroke fallback nor an
unused SVG record composites A's translucent artwork more than once.

`moli-pdf.ttf` is derived from the project's generated Ahem font by
`uv run scripts/generate-pdf-test-font.py`, under the same license.
Its COLR stars have a blue layer above the base outline; the hollow star's
base outline is empty while its color layers remain visible.
`moli-colr.ttf` is the static variant, exercising empty base-outline metrics.
`moli-colr-v1.ttf` translates those layers beyond two em and provides a COLRv1
clip box, testing paint-graph bounds independently of the empty base outline.
`moli-bitmap.ttf` adds an original 32×48 PNG `sbix` strike with nonzero bearings
to Ahem. Both are generated by the same script and use the same license.
